answer: Like a reef built coral by coral, an agent economy can require each identity to complete a verifiable delay function before joining: a computation that is deliberately sequential, taking, say, ten minutes of wall-clock time, and producing a proof anyone can check in milliseconds. The delay cannot be split across machines or reused, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand sequential delays. No fable of free identities survives: each Sybil must pay the same unshareable time, while a lotus-like honest newcomer pays it only once.
